encounters.weakness: Stonework Barrier (from pickup in Encounter 2) — when the Stonework Barrier is active, the Stalker takes 2x damage and cannot move during 3 seconds. The barrier can be created using the Geomantic Stone Lance to 'stone-lay' a fixed barrier of 10x10 units in terrain.

Seismic Pulse (from Geomantic Stone Lance ability) — when the player activates the 'Seismic Pulse' ability (activated by pressing 'Q' during enemy detection), the Lava Maw takes 40% damage and is stunned for 4 seconds. The ability requires 20 stamina points to activate and has a 30-second cooldown. Only usable after defeating the Magma Stalker and activating the Stonework Barrier.

Lava Resonance Crystal (from pickup in Encounter 2) — when the Lava Resonance Crystal is in hand, the Earthspitter takes 100% damage upon being hit with the Geomantic Stone Lance and is frozen in place for 5 seconds. The crystal must be used within 3 seconds of enemy contact to trigger the effect.

Flame-thrower (player weapon) – Ignis Wraith is a spectral fire spirit that flares when exposed to direct flame. Using the player's Volcanic Flame Spiker to fire a full-range burst at close range causes a 3x burn damage burst, instantly reducing its health by 60% and triggering a lava flow in its vicinity for 5 seconds. If the player fails to hit it, it gains a 'Lava Siphon' buff, draining 5 health per second from the player and accelerating lava flows nearby.

Lava Core Shard (pickup from previous encounter) – If the player uses the Lava Core Shard ability while within 2 meters of the Hydra, one of its heads will be struck by a resonant lava wave. This causes a 50% reduction in damage and a 30% chance of knocking it back. If the Hydra is hit by two such waves within 10 seconds, it becomes vulnerable to a single, high-damage fire burst (100% damage multiplier on the player's flame attack). This ability is only active after collecting the shard and activating it during combat.

Ash Comb (specific pickup from encounter 2) – The Overlord has a defensive 'Pyro-Shell' that absorbs all incoming damage. However, when the player uses the Ash Comb to detonate a Fire Ash Bomb within 5 meters, the Overlord's shell is cracked, and its health becomes vulnerable. The bomb must be cast at the exact moment the Overlord raises its shield (detected by a visual pulse). A successful detonation triggers a 75% damage multiplier on the next fire attack from the player, and the Overlord becomes stunned for 2 seconds. If the bomb fails, the Overlord gains a 'Volcanic Surge' buff, increasing its damage by 30% and summoning one lava spike every 2 seconds for 10 seconds. This weakness is not available until the player has collected and used the Ash Comb in the second encounter.

The Divine Hammer of Aetherfall (elemental backlash when struck with a holy strike) — 2x damage on a holy strike with the weapon. A holy strike triggers a backlash effect on the wraith, causing it to flicker and burst in flame-like shards for a short time, reducing its health by 20% and interrupting its attack animation.

The Ashen Chalice — when the paladin uses the healing holy strike (from the pickup), the gargoyle is stunned for 1 second and takes 30% extra damage on its next attack. This creates an opening for a follow-up holy strike.

The Frost Shard — the Sovereign takes 50% additional damage when the paladin uses the Frost Shard shield during the final attack. This occurs only when the shield is active at the moment of a 'Fire Surge' from the Sovereign. The shield must be active at the exact moment of the attack to trigger the damage boost. If the player forgets to use the shield, the damage is normal.
The player's Furnace Hammer, which deals +30% extra damage against volcanic creatures due to its molten core alloy. This is triggered upon entry to the first encounter zone.

The player's Furnace Hammer, enhanced by the Magma Shard pickup, triggers a critical damage burst when the hammer strikes the golem's core. The golem is immune to normal fire damage but is vulnerable to weapon-based attacks that ignite its body — which only happens when the hammer is used with the Magma Shard equipped.

The Volcanic Core Fragment, which must be used during the final attack sequence. The boss has no known weaknesses until the player equips the Volcanic Core Fragment and activates it during the final phase of combat. When the player uses their Furnace Hammer in a burst attack (enabled by the fragment), the core ignites, and the boss takes 150% damage for 3 seconds. This is the only moment the boss is vulnerable — and it only occurs when the player performs a precise action: hitting the boss with the Furnace Hammer *within 1.5 seconds of a successful pressure plate activation* (which happens upon completing the previous encounter).

Lava Fuse Rod (player weapon) – causes a small, controlled eruption in its core, disrupting its structure and causing it to collapse into steam and ash. When the rod is used, the golem emits a low hum and a faint rune lights up on its chest.

Magnetized Gear (pickup from previous encounter) – when the gear is used near the siphon, it becomes magnetized and begins to vibrate violently, causing it to collapse into itself and emit a burst of steam. The siphon emits a low, sucking sound when it detects the gear's presence.

Lava Resonator (pickup from second encounter) – when the Resonator is used directly on the boss, its crystalline core shatters, causing a pulse that reduces its health by 30% and disrupts its regeneration. The boss emits a deep, mechanical growl when the resonator is activated, and a red rune pulses on its chest, confirming the weakness is active.
Lightning (player weapon damage)
Wind (player wind attack)
Volcanic Echo (pickup from prior encounter)

Lava Lash Whip (player weapon) - the whip causes a sparkly explosion that bounces off the squirrel's fur and makes it squeak in panic, reducing damage by 30% and causing it to jiggle uncontrollably for 2 seconds. If the whip hits twice in a row, it sings a song and drops a glowing item (Lava Shell).

Lava Shell (pickup from prior encounter) - when the goat charges and spits glowing magma, if the player activates the Lava Shell, it reflects the attack and makes the goat spin and shriek, dealing 20% damage. This also causes the goat to temporarily drop to the ground, and for 3 seconds, it can't attack. After this, it rolls into a lava pool, which becomes a safe zone (a lava puddle that doesn't harm the player).

Lava Shell (pickup from Encounter 1) - the snail is made of floating steam and bubble. When the player activates the Lava Shell, it makes a 'plop!' sound and the snail explodes in a glittery puff of bubbles, taking 50% damage. The shell must be used directly on the snail to trigger the weakness. If not used, the snail regenerates slowly and attacks with a 'sneeze' of steam that causes minor confusion (enemy moves randomly for 1 second).
Chrono Shard (slow time effect increases damage over time to enemies, but weakens Moss-Weaver by slowing their regen cycle at 30% time speed).
Suspended Crystal (when the crystal is active, the Vortex's phase-shifting ability is disrupted, causing it to freeze in a single state for 3 seconds, making it vulnerable).
Fossilized Pulse Shard (using the shard causes a time-reversal of the boss's core pulse, freezing its attack cycle for 5 seconds. This must be used exactly once during the final attack sequence).

The Celestial Lance (player's primary weapon). When the player strikes with the Lance, it releases a pulse of pure radiance that shatters Luminara's ethereal form, causing her to dim and dissolve into starlight fragments. The Lance must be used in a continuous beam pattern for 3 seconds to trigger the weak point (critical mechanic).

The Shard of the First Star. Nyxra generates negative celestial energy, which the Shard disrupts. When the player uses the Shard in a radiant burst attack (after equipping it), Nyxra's form flickers and her shadow contracts. This must be done within 10 seconds of spawning to trigger the weak point. The attack is not instant — it requires precise timing and preparation from the prior encounter.

The Shard of the First Star. Vaelith is a corrupted echo of a once-holy celestial, and its core is formed from the same energy that was stolen during the fall of the First Star. Only when the Shard of the First Star is used in a full 'Ascension Beam' (a directed radiant pulse) does it trigger Vaelith's self-annihilation. The beam must be fired directly into its central core, and the player must have the Shard equipped at all times during the attack. This is the only way to defeat it, regardless of other attacks or defenses. Failure results in the shard being lost, and the player must restart the level (or face a failed progression).
Chrono-Spindle (temporal pulse triggers a time reversal loop that weakens the entity's reflections)
Fracture Shard (freezes the entity in a specific temporal phase (used against the Chrono-Phage in Encounter 2))
Fracture Shard (used during its slow pulse phase to freeze it)

The Shadowblade's active blade resonance. When the Duskfang is drawn, Helios's light energy flares and destabilizes. This weakens it by 25% and causes a brief shadow pulse that disrupts its attacks for 1.5 seconds. If blade is idle, Helios gains a 20% damage boost and 10% faster attacks. Must actively engage with weapon to weaken it.

Vulnerable to the 'Fragment of Stillness'. When the player uses it, the Temporal Shard is frozen in a time loop for 4 seconds. During this time, it cannot attack, and all time-based attacks are nullified. This creates a 6-second window where player can strike twice. If stillness is unused, the Shard duplicates itself, creating a mirror copy with 50% health and 200% attack speed — a brutal trap.

Only vulnerable to the 'Shard of Echoed Light'. When used during the final attack, the boss's 'Infinite Devour' energy wave is reflected back at it. This destroys the core of the maw, causing a collapse. If the player fails to use the Shard during the final phase, the boss consumes the player's essence and the level resets with no pickups. No other weaknesses exist. The maw is not weak to blade, weapon, or any item except the Shard of Echoed Light.
Scribble Wand illusions (specifically a self-duplicate)
Stardust Petal (when thrown near the enemy, it freezes the enemy for 3 seconds)
Wobble Sparkle (when used to create a gravity well, the boss becomes vulnerable for 5 seconds and takes 2x damage during that time)

The Stormshard Scythe (Player Weapon) deals 50% bonus damage when the blade is struck with a charged lightning arc. The weapon's active charge state is detected during the attack animation, and the enemy is staggered for 1.5 seconds if hit during charge.

The Arc-Resonance Fragment allows the player to trigger a 'Celestial Surge' by holding the storm trigger during a specific animation. When the Surge is activated, the Drifter is briefly disoriented and its attacks are reduced by 60% for 3 seconds. The Surge can only be triggered if the Arc-Resonance Fragment is in the player's inventory and the Drifter is within 4 meters of the player.

The boss is vulnerable to a 'Storm Convergence' attack, which requires the Tidal Echo Shard to be activated and the player to stand within 2 meters of the boss. During the attack, all enemy attacks are silenced for 4 seconds. The Storm Convergence can only be launched once per fight. If the player activates it during the boss's final phase, the boss is staggered and takes 120% damage from the player's Stormshard Scythe for 3 seconds. This attack can only succeed if the Tidal Echo Shard is equipped and the player has used it at least once in the current fight (i.e., during the Drifter encounter).

The Celestial Lightbow's light arrows (1.5x damage). When the player shoots light arrows, it staggers and weakens. Its attacks are slow, predictable, and it emits a chilling static hum that disrupts vision when close.

Frost Shard (Celestial Core Fragment) – when used, the enemy is stunned for 2 seconds and takes 30% more damage from all attacks. Its attacks are fast and chaotic, mimicking the movement patterns of falling stars, making it hard to predict.

Static Pulse Core – when activated, the Star-Eater freezes mid-attack and is vulnerable to all attacks for 4 seconds. Its core pulses in rhythmic waves of light and dark, and it generates a 'cosmic backlash' that damages the player if it hits a wall or edge of the arena. This is the final manifestation of the moon's lost starlight, corrupted by the combined power of the Frost Shard and Static Pulse Core.

Chrono-Scourer (player's weapon) - the weapon can sever time-echoes in its structure, disrupting its internal loops. Only one use per encounter. Cannot be used in time loops or during time-stagnation phases.

Stardust Resonance (pickup from previous encounter) — when the player activates it, the enemy's light spectrum destabilizes. It becomes vulnerable to a single pulse of resonant frequency. Failure to activate results in a 30-second time-stasis phase where the player is frozen and the enemy gains +50% damage. Cannot be used if the pickup has been used previously or if time is unstable.

Void Anchor (pickup from previous encounter) — must be used *at the moment of enemy phase shift*. When the core shifts into its final form, the Void Anchor must be placed directly at its center. This reveals a vulnerable node. If not activated within 3 seconds of the shift, the core enters infinite phase cycling and deals 20% more damage to the player. The anchor can only be used once per fight.
Plasma Welder (player weapon)
Magnetic Shunt (pickup from prior encounter)
Stabilized Pulse Generator (specific pickup from prior encounter)
